message.content: In lions, the most well‑known dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene that controls mane development (and its size and density) is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male inherits the allele from either parent, he will develop a mane. This trait is strongly influenced by testosterone levels, but genetically it follows a classic dominant pattern.
